problem:
The cubic polynomial $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=3,{x}_{2,3}=1\pm 2\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $6.$ Find $f(x).$

$P(x)=$
{{field-1}}${x}^{3}\,-$
{{field-2}}${x}^{2}\,+$
{{field-3}}$x\,-$
{{field-4}}
worked_solution:
Since $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2,3}=1\pm 2\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=6,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) \\  & =6(x-3)(x-(1+2\text{i}))(x-(1-2\text{i}))\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}6(x-3)(x-(1+2\text{i}))(x-(1-2\text{i})) & = \\ 6(x-3)({x}^{2}-x(1+2\text{i})-x(1-2\text{i})+(1+2\text{i})(1-2\text{i})) & = \\ 6(x-3)({x}^{2}-2x+5) & = \\ 6({x}^{3}-5{x}^{2}+11x-15) & = \\ 6{x}^{3}-30{x}^{2}+66x-90.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=6{x}^{3}-30{x}^{2}+66x-90.$
